newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sells $8.77 mln fishing plant to local firm.
newsitem.headline: Peru sells $8.77 mln fishing plant to local firm.

text.p: Peru's state fishing company Pescaperu sold its Tambo de Mora fishing plant at an auction Monday for $8.77 million to local firm Pesquera Maria del Milagro, privatization officials said.
Three firms competed at the auction, whose minimum bid price was $4.25 million. But details of the other two offers for the plant, 125 miles (200 km) south of Lima, were unavailable.
The government has four more plants to sell to complete its piecemeal privatization of Pescaperu's assets.
Each of the four plants will be sold at a "bargain" price of $3.5 million because of their environmental liabilities, Pescaperu's privatization chief, Dante Matelini, said.
The government has received over $120 million from the sale of fishing assets since it began in 1994 the privatization of the sector, which is Peru's second largest industry after mining.
